deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §4.3 of Grothendieck's 'laïus' on crystals (Nov.–Dec. 1966). On the previous page he stated the theorem: if S has characteristic 0 and X is smooth over S, then the cohomology of the structure sheaf on the crystalline or stratifying site of X/S equals relative algebraic de Rham cohomology, H^*_{cris/strat}(X/S, O_X) ≃ H^*_{DR}(X/S). 'Ceci donnera une explication' says this result will explain the following conjecture.

Conjecture: let X be locally of finite type over C, possibly singular. Then H^*_{strat or cris}(X/C, O_X) ≃ H^*(X^{an}, C). In modern terms, the cohomology of O on the infinitesimal site computes the singular cohomology of the associated analytic space. Over Q, divided powers on nilpotent ideals exist automatically, so the crystalline site in characteristic 0 is essentially the infinitesimal site. The stratifying site gives the same cohomology.

N.B.: in the smooth case the conjecture follows by combining two results. The first is the theorem just stated (cris/strat equals DR). The second is the comparison theorem of 'exposé 1', namely Grothendieck's 1966 algebraic de Rham theorem H^*_{DR}(X/C) ≃ H^*(X^{an}, C) for smooth X. Hence, for smooth X, one gets a description of de Rham cohomology without using differential forms (underlined).

The purpose is to motivate the crystalline/infinitesimal topos as the correct de Rham-type theory for singular varieties, intrinsic and free of differentials. It also serves as the characteristic-0 model for the p-adic crystalline programme.
errors: No mathematical error. The conjecture is true: Grothendieck sketched it in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) by embedding X in a smooth Y and using the formally completed de Rham complex. Hartshorne treated the formal-completion de Rham theory in detail (Publ. IHES 45, 1975). The deduction in the smooth case is correct as stated.
Minor imprecision only: 'locally of finite type' with no separatedness assumption is fine for this statement.

ideas.what: For X locally of finite type over C, possibly singular, the infinitesimal/crystalline (or stratifying) cohomology of O_X equals the singular cohomology of X^an with C coefficients.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorem for infinitesimal cohomology (singular algebraic de Rham theorem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Hartshorne (1975) for the formal-completion de Rham version
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', §4

ideas.what: Smooth case deduced from crystalline/stratifying = de Rham plus the algebraic de Rham comparison theorem; yields de Rham cohomology without differentials.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham comparison theorem; infinitesimal cohomology = de Rham cohomology in the smooth case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material Grothendieck published essentially verbatim in the 1968 'Crystals' paper, and the conjecture is well known and proven. The page is historically interesting only as showing the statement still labelled a conjecture in late 1966.
transcription_corrections: The subscript of H^* in the conjecture is not 'DR'. It reads 'Str' (strat), apparently overwritten or struck, with 'ou crist.' written beneath. So the statement is H^*_{strat ou crist}(X/C, O_X) ≃ H^*(X^an, C). A 'DR' subscript would make the singular case meaningless and contradict the N.B.
'grâce au th., [-lorsque-], [-d-] au th. de comparaison' is more plausibly 'grâce au th., [-toujours-], [-d-] joint au th. de comparaison de l'exposé 1'.

The last sentence probably reads: 'Donc dans le cas lisse, on [-dispose-] trouve une description de la coh. de D.R. sans utilisation de différentielles.' The latter part, from 'dans le cas lisse' to the end, is underlined.
